rationale: The buyer is a concrete, nameable prosumer — freelance devs and small teams paying $20-200/month for AI coding subscriptions — who demonstrably spends money on tooling and has a live cost-tracking problem. Buildability is solid (a lightweight dashboard reading API usage logs via Claude + a simple web page + Stripe) and the service could run autonomously once configured. The main gaps are: willingness_to_pay sits at the floor (people pay for the subscriptions but haven't yet been shown to pay separately for analytics of them), responsiveness is untested, and defensibility is low. Validate with a landing page and 20 outreach messages to power users in indie-hacker communities before committing to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an AI-spend analytics dashboard for solo developers: it ingests API usage logs (Claude, OpenAI, Copilot) and shows spend broken down by repo, task type, or session, with a monthly cost-vs-output report. BUILD: the factory creates a Claude prompt pipeline that parses uploaded usage CSVs or connects via API key, generates a weekly spend digest, and hosts a simple read-only dashboard; payment is a $15/month Stripe link; signup is a one-page form. SELL: outreach targets power users in the Indie Hackers forum, r/MachineLearning, and dev.to 'AI tools' tag — a list of 100+ qualified names is reachable in under a week; the factory drafts the outreach and the operator approves the send batch. MAINTAIN: digest generation, support Q&A (via Claude), and billing renewals all run automatically; the only recurring human step is approving outreach batches and reviewing any refund requests. CAVEAT: willingness-to-pay is unconfirmed — validate with a 'join the waitlist for $15/mo' page before building the full dashboard.
notes: All build_gates met (operational_autonomy 7, buildability_with_ai 7, buyer_clarity 6, willingness_to_pay 5), but total (5.7) is below min_total_to_build (6.5), so stage is correctly validate. Defensibility is low (3) — this is a commodity layer once a larger player notices the gap.
